#Loading the data
Make sure that the previous file has been run and has saved the rds
 files (GSE270199_imputed.rds & GSE270199_redmeta.rds found 
 in the OUTPUTS location)

#The general pipeline in this file
* Get a *similarity network* for the patients
* *Cluster* the patients using the similarity network
* Perform *Wilcoxon rank-sum test* on each feature
  --> p-value
  * Correct using *FDR*
* Get *log2FC* of each cluster vs the other using the median 
   to better deal with outliers
  --> log2FC
  * Two ways:
      - *Compare the cluster to each other directly* 
        --> Up- / Downregulated in one group over the other
        --> Presumably gives less overlap as the nodes used for 
             diffusion cannot overlap to begin with (either up- or 
             downregulated)
      - (Not implemented) Compare the clusters to the controls and 
         then to each other
        --> (Not implemented) Up- / Downregulated in reference to 
             the controls, can then compare those to each other 
        --> (Not implemented) Presumably finds more shared areas as 
             a node can be up- / downregulated in both of the comparisons 
             before the diffusion comparison between the groups
* Get a *selection of genes* to use for the network diffusion using filters
  * Get protein codes to give to STRING instead of ENSG codes
* Use *PCA* on only the EDS samples to build a *background network* 
   that the selected nodes are diffused over
  * Get protein codes to give to STRING instead of ENSG codes
* *Diffuse* over the network and compare the clusters to each other
  --> Unique nodes for one cluster?
  --> Nodes that both clusters diffused to?
    * *INTERPRET*:
      --> Unique nodes (only up or only down) could imply a different 
           area of origin for some of the effects
      --> Shared diffused-to nodes could show that despite originating 
           from different nodes, the same area of the PPI may be affected

#Build a similarity network and cut into clusters
Build a similarity network, 
  first for all the samples for exploration
  then with the '700 sample' removed as it simply acts too much like an outlier
  then with just the EDS samples, as that is what we want to cluster
  then with the clusters visualized
```{r similarity_network}
#Get some group information that can be used for color labels
healthy_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("healthy", metadata[,"disease_state"])]
EDS_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("EDS-HT", metadata[,"disease_state"])]
Male_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("Male", metadata[,"inferred_sex"])]
Female_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("Female", metadata[,"inferred_sex"])]

if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #Using all the data
  Fun_heatmap(data_matrix = t(data),
              SAVE_PLOT = TRUE,
              title = "Heatmap of all the data",

              xlab = "Sex",

              ylab = "Disease")


  #Without GSM8336700
    #700 keeps acting like an outlier, wanted to see how the similarity would look without it
  Fun_heatmap(data_matrix = t(data[,colnames(data) != "GSM8336700"]),
              SAVE_PLOT = TRUE,
              title = "Without GSM8336700",
              col_side = "sex",
              xlab = "Sex",
              row_side = "disease",
              ylab = "Disease")

```

```{r clusters}
#Use the same code inside the function to get the clusters out and into the metadata
#Compute similarity using correlation
#Correlation as I want to compare patterns
sim_obj <- simil(t(data[,EDS_group]), 
                  method = "correlation",
                  pairwise = TRUE) 
#Convert to a matrix 
sim_matrix <- as.matrix(sim_obj)
#Set the self-correlation to 1 as the function gives a self correlation of zero back
diag(sim_matrix) <- 1

#Get out some clusters by creating a dist_matrix as well
dist_matrix <- 1-sim_matrix
diag(dist_matrix) <- 0
dist_matrix <- as.dist(dist_matrix)
  
#Get dendrogram
hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "complete")

#Cut into 2 clusters
clusters_k <- cutree(hc, 2)
clusters_k <- as.data.frame(clusters_k)
#Set the controls to cluster 0 so that the information can be added to the broader metadata file
clusters_k[healthy_group,] <- 0

#Add the cluster information to the metadata
metadata <- merge(metadata, clusters_k, by = "row.names")
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$Row.names
metadata$Row.names <- NULL

#Remove unneeded objects to clean the global environment
rm(hc, sim_matrix, dist_matrix, sim_obj)
```


#wilcox.test
Performing a wilcox test to find p_values between the clusters 
  Note to myself: I tested if the results of the p-values would change if I unlogged the data, the p-values seem to stay the same as this source also mentions (https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/178744/how-do-logarithmic-measurements-affect-the-wilcoxon-rank-sum-test)
```{r wilcox_test}
#NOTE: I would have preferred to turn this into a more modular function so it could handle more than two clusters dynamically, but considering that only two clusters are selected this was sufficient for now

#Get cluster identifiers inside a list
  #This was an initial step to making the code more modular
  #The length of the list is dependent on the amount of unique values in metadata[,"clusters_k"] minus 1 (to account for the cluster 0 controls)
cluster_list <- list()
for (cluster in 1:(length(unique(metadata[,"clusters_k"]))-1)){
cluster_list[[paste0("cluster_",cluster,"_group")]] <- rownames(metadata)[grep(cluster, metadata[,"clusters_k"])]
}

#Set up cluster_1_vs_2 to save the p-value and statistic results
cluster_1_vs_2 <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = nrow(data), ncol = 2))
rownames(cluster_1_vs_2) <- rownames(data)
colnames(cluster_1_vs_2) <- c("p_value","statistic")

for (i in 1:nrow(data)){
  #Use the two.sided setting as the goal is not to check if one is greater/less than the other but to see if either one of them are different from the other
  res <- wilcox.test((as.double(data[i,unname(unlist(cluster_list[1]))])), 
                     (as.double(data[i,unname(unlist(cluster_list[2]))])), 
                     paired = FALSE, 
                     alternative = "two.sided")
  #Save the result
  cluster_1_vs_2[i,"p_value"] <- res$p.value
  cluster_1_vs_2[i,"statistic"] <- res$statistic
}

#Also add an adjusted p value using FDR
cluster_1_vs_2[,"adj_p_value"] <- p.adjust(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"], method = 'fdr', n = length(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"]))


#Give some feedback
cat(paste0(sum(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"] < 0.05), 
           " (",
           round((sum(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"] < 0.05)/nrow(cluster_1_vs_2))*100,2),
           "%) made it to a p-value of 0.05 or below between the two clusters."))


#Remove unneeded objects to clean the global environment
rm(res, cluster, i, clusters_k)

```
#Get log2FC between the clusters
The formula used to calculate the fold change was found at:
https://www.biostars.org/p/342756/
  --> mean(log2(Group1)) - mean(log2(Group2))
    --> median(log2(Group1)) - median(log2(Group2))
Calculating both as median can handle outliers better on advice from Agi
```{r log2FC}
#As it was assumed that the data was already in log2 notation, the log2FC should be as simple as taking the mean/median and subtracting

#Get the median of the clusters and place it in a df
data.cluster <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = nrow(data),ncol = 0))
rownames(data.cluster) <- rownames(data)

for (i in 1:nrow(data)){
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_mean"] <- mean(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_1_group]))
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_mean"] <- mean(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_2_group]))
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_median"] <- median(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_1_group]))
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_median"] <- median(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_2_group]))
}

#Get the log2FC by subtracting the mean(log2()) / median(log2()) clusters
for (i in 1:nrow(data.cluster)){
  data.cluster[i,"log2FC_mean"] <- data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_mean"] - data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_mean"]
  data.cluster[i,"log2FC_median"] <- data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_median"] - data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_median"]
}

#Print some feedback
head(data.cluster)

#Remove unneeded objects to clean the global environment
rm(i, cluster_list)
```
#Combine the results
Combine the p value and log2FC results into one df
```{r initial_results}
#Set the results, together with the previously found p values to a df
data.results <- merge(data.cluster[,c("log2FC_mean", "log2FC_median")], cluster_1_vs_2[,c("p_value","adj_p_value")], by = "row.names")
rownames(data.results) <- data.results$Row.names
data.results$Row.names <- NULL

#Remove some of the loose objects
rm(cluster_1_vs_2, data.cluster)
```

#Filter for the data to actually use
```{r}
#If the fold change is below 1, I disregard that measure as the change is less than doubled or halved
  #This allows me to reduce the amount of data I am dealing with 
  # (as úsing, for example, 0.58 creates a URI to long error when sending the command to Cytoscape)
  #Using the median because as far as I am aware it is better with dealing with outliers
data.selected <- data.results[abs(data.results[,"log2FC_median"]) > 1,]

#Get quantiles of the adj_p_value
  #I would like to take along at least 25% of the data so that I make sure I don't cut out too much
  #type = 7 is the default, this default is makes use of linear interpolation. I did not change away from the default.
cat("What the adjusted pvalues are at these probabilities:\n")
quantile(data.selected[,"adj_p_value"],
         type = 7,
         probs = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 25, 50, 75, 100)/100)
pvalue_cutoff <- quantile(data.selected[,"adj_p_value"],
                           type = 7,
                           probs = 25/100)
cat("\nThe adjusted pvalue at 25%: ",pvalue_cutoff,"\n")

data.selected <- data.selected[data.selected[,"adj_p_value"] <= pvalue_cutoff,]


#print some feedback
cat(nrow(data.selected), "genes made it through the selection.\n")

#Convert to something that STRING can work with better
selected_proteins <- gconvert(rownames(data.selected),
                              organism="hsapiens",
                              target="ENTREZGENE",
                              filter_na = F)$target
selected_proteins <- selected_proteins[!is.na(selected_proteins)]

selected_proteins_up <- gconvert(rownames(data.selected[data.selected["log2FC_median"]>0,]),
                                 organism="hsapiens",
                                 target="ENTREZGENE",
                                 filter_na = F)$target
selected_proteins_up <- selected_proteins_up[!is.na(selected_proteins_up)]

selected_proteins_down <- gconvert(rownames(data.selected[data.selected["log2FC_median"]<0,]),
                                 organism="hsapiens",
                                 target="ENTREZGENE",
                                 filter_na = F)$target
selected_proteins_down <- selected_proteins_down[!is.na(selected_proteins_down)]


#Print some feedback
cat(length(selected_proteins),"protein names selected to use in the network.\n")
cat(length(selected_proteins_up),"protein names are upregulated.\n")
cat(length(selected_proteins_down),"protein names are downregulated.\n")



#Clean the global environment
rm(pvalue_cutoff)

```

#PCA on only the EDS samples
Display the PCA's that are used to build the background network with and then select the genes that are used to build the STRING background network.
```{r pca_on_disease}
#Subset to only get the patient data
data.disease_only <- data[,EDS_group]

#Run a PCA on the patient only data
PCA.disease_only <- pca(object = t(as.matrix(data.disease_only)), 
                   method = "svd", nPcs = 10, center = TRUE)


if (!USE_CUMULATIVE_VARIANCE){
  cat("The PC's that have 10% or more variance:\n")
  print(PCA.disease_only@R2[PCA.disease_only@R2 > 0.10])
  pca_variance_selection <- names(PCA.disease_only@R2[PCA.disease_only@R2 > 0.10])
} else if (USE_CUMULATIVE_VARIANCE){
  cat("The PC's that have a cumulative 90% variance:\n")
  print(PCA.disease_only@R2cum[1:(sum(PCA.disease_only@R2cum <= 0.9)+1)])
  pca_variance_selection <- names(PCA.disease_only@R2cum[1:(sum(PCA.disease_only@R2cum <= 0.9)+1)])
} else {
  warning("Something unknown went wrong, stopping code.\n")
  stop()
}

if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #Visualize the PC's that have 10 or more % variance
  for (PC in 1:length(pca_variance_selection)){
    #PC1 and PC2 are not the clearest variable names to use here, not sure what else could work better though
    PC1 <- pca_variance_selection[PC]
    ifelse(PC != length(pca_variance_selection),
           PC2 <- pca_variance_selection[PC+1],
           PC2 <- pca_variance_selection[1])

    Fun_plot_PCA_scores(PCA = PCA.disease_only, 
                      metadata = metadata, 
                      SAVE_PLOT = TRUE,
                      firstPC = PC1, 
                      secondPC = PC2, 
                      title = paste0("PCA scores (",PC1," vs ",PC2,") of just the patients"))

  }
} else {
  cat("Plot not visualized due to RUN_PLOTS being set to FALSE.\n")
}

#Extract the top genes for the selected PC's
background_nodes <- NULL
for (PC in 1:length(pca_variance_selection)){
  #Get the 99% value and use it as the threshold
    #Above this value should contain the top 1% of the data that is important for the loadings of this PC
      #This value is chosen somewhat arbitrarily but ensures that not too many genes are chosen
      # Selecting more genes produces more genes than can be sent to Cytoscape in a single command
  threshold <- quantile(abs(PCA.disease_only@loadings[,pca_variance_selection[PC]]),
                         type = 7,
                         probs = 99/100,
                         names = FALSE)

  passed <- abs(PCA.disease_only@loadings[,pca_variance_selection[PC]]) >= threshold
  
  #Save the nodes that are in the top percent
  background_nodes <- c(background_nodes, rownames(PCA.disease_only@loadings[passed,]))
}
#Use unique to remove duplicates
background_nodes <- unique(background_nodes)

cat("Selected", length(background_nodes),"genes to build the background network with.\n")


#Convert to something that STRING can work with better
background_proteins <- gconvert(background_nodes,organism="hsapiens",target="ENTREZGENE",filter_na = F)$target
background_proteins <- background_proteins[!is.na(background_proteins)]

cat(length(background_proteins),"protein names selected to build the background network with.\n")


#Clean the environment
rm(passed, threshold, PC, PC1, PC2, pca_variance_selection)

```

#Build the Cytoscape selected network
This is to see if the nodes that were found connect in a decent way, even without allowing to addition of more nodes (limit=0).
```{r cytoscape_selected_network}
#Visualize the selected nodes in a separate Cytoscape network
if (VISUALIZE_SELECTED_NETWORK){
#Build the command to send to Cytoscape
  #use the same low cutoff (0.4)
cmd <- paste0(
  'string protein query ',
  'query=', paste(selected_proteins, collapse = ", "), ' ',
  'networkType=physical subnetwork ',
  'cutoff=0.4 ',
  'newNetName=Selected Network ',
  'species="Homo sapiens" ',
  'limit=0 ',
  'showFlatNodeDesign=true ',
  'showSTRINGstyleLabels=false ',
  'showStructureImages=false'
  )

#Send the command to Cytoscape to build the network
RCy3::commandsRun(cmd)

#Get the network's SUID
selected_networkSuid = getNetworkSuid()
}
```

#Build the Cytoscape background network
```{r cytoscape_background_network}
#Build the command to send to Cytoscape
  #use a low cutoff (0.4)
  #Allow the network to expand by 10% of the queried proteins to get a more connected picture
cmd <- paste0(
  'string protein query ',
  'query=', paste(background_proteins, collapse = ", "), ' ',
  'networkType=physical subnetwork ',
  'cutoff=0.4 ',
  'newNetName="Background Network" ',
  'species="Homo sapiens" ',
  'limit=', round(length(background_proteins)*0.1),' ',
  'showFlatNodeDesign=true ',
  'showSTRINGstyleLabels=false ',
  'showStructureImages=false'
  )

#Send the command to Cytoscape to build the network
RCy3::commandsRun(cmd)

#Get the network's SUID
background_networkSuid = getNetworkSuid()



#Ensure the optimal zoom
RCy3::fitContent(network = background_networkSuid)

#Get the filename
file_name <- paste0(OUTPUT_FILE_LOCATION,"/Cytoscape_initial_STRING")

#Export a PNG of the network
RCy3::exportImage(filename = file_name,
                  type = "PNG",
                  resolution = 600, #600 should be the maximum allowed
                  units = "inches", #inches should make the file larger
                  zoom = 500, #Use the maximum zoom possible
                  network = background_networkSuid,
                  overwriteFile = TRUE #It is allowed to overwrite the previous file (Default)
)


```

#Diffusion
Diffuse the proteins that were found in the selected set over the network created from the background set.
```{r diffusion}
#NOTE: I would have preferred to turn this into a function so it could handle more than two clusters dynamically, but considering that only two clusters are selected this was sufficient for now


#Get pre-allocated object to save the diffusion output that can be merged into
  #display name and query term are loaded in so that the merge command can merge the dataframes using that as a reference
diffusion_output <- getTableColumns(
    table = "node",
    columns = c("display name","query term"),
    network = background_networkSuid
)


#Select up nodes in Cytoscape network
selectNodes(
    selected_proteins_up,
    by.col = "display name",
    preserve.current.selection = FALSE,
    network = background_networkSuid
)

#Diffuse from the up nodes
#Diffusion time of 0.5 selected to not only find direct neighbors, but also nodes a few edges further
RCy3::commandsRun('diffusion diffuse_advanced time=0.5')

#Rename the diffusion output so that the results don't get mixed up
renameTableColumn(
    table = "node",
    column = "diffusion_output_heat",
    new.name = "up_heat",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
renameTableColumn(
    table = "node",
    column = "diffusion_output_rank",
    new.name = "up_rank",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
renameTableColumn(
    table = "node",
    column = "diffusion_input",
    new.name = "up_diffusion_input",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
  
#Get the diffusion results from Cytoscape
temp_output <- getTableColumns(
    table = "node",
    columns = c("display name","query term", "up_heat", "up_rank", "up_diffusion_input"),
    network = background_networkSuid
)

#Round the output to both filter out extremely low heat and make downstream easier
temp_output["up_heat"] <- round(temp_output["up_heat"], 2)

#Remove the NA's from diffusion_input
temp_output[is.na(temp_output["up_diffusion_input"]),"up_diffusion_input"] <- 0

#Merge the new result to the diffusion_output
diffusion_output <- merge(diffusion_output, temp_output)


#Select down nodes in Cytoscape network
selectNodes(
    selected_proteins_down,
    by.col = "display name",
    preserve.current.selection = FALSE,
    network = background_networkSuid
)

#Diffuse from the down nodes
#Diffusion time of 0.5 selected to not only find direct neighbors, but also nodes a few edges further
RCy3::commandsRun('diffusion diffuse_advanced time=0.5')

#Rename the diffusion output so that the results don't get mixed up
renameTableColumn(
    table = "node",
    column = "diffusion_output_heat",
    new.name = "down_heat",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
renameTableColumn(
    table = "node",
    column = "diffusion_output_rank",
    new.name = "down_rank",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
renameTableColumn(
    table = "node",
    column = "diffusion_input",
    new.name = "down_diffusion_input",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
  
#Get the diffusion results from Cytoscape
temp_output <- getTableColumns(
    table = "node",
    columns = c("display name","query term", "down_heat", "down_rank", "down_diffusion_input"),
    network = background_networkSuid
)

#Round the output to both filter out extremely low heat and make downstream easier
temp_output["down_heat"] <- round(temp_output["down_heat"], 2)
#Remove the NA's from diffusion_input
temp_output[is.na(temp_output["down_diffusion_input"]),"down_diffusion_input"] <- 0

#Merge the new result to the diffusion_output
diffusion_output <- merge(diffusion_output, temp_output)

#Print some feedback
head(diffusion_output)


#Clean the environment
rm(temp_output)
```
#Diffusion processing
Process the information that came out of the diffusion and send that info back to Cytoscape for visualization options.
```{r diffusion_processing}
#Get up and down out for ease
up <- diffusion_output$up_heat
down <- diffusion_output$down_heat

#Get the overlap and difference between the two diffusions
results <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = length(up), ncol = 0))
rownames(results) <- diffusion_output$"display name"
results$difference <- up - down
results$abs_difference <- abs(results$difference)
results$input <- diffusion_output$up_diffusion_input + diffusion_output$down_diffusion_input

#Make a comparison and use an offset so that nodes that are very similar are also considered equal
results$direction <- ifelse(up <= 0.01 & down <= 0.01,
                            #Neither of them carry enough heat to be considered
                            "No heat",
                             ifelse(round(abs(up - down),5) <= 0.01,
                                    #Up and down are considered equal,
                                    "Equal",
                                    ifelse(up <= 0.01 & down > 0.01,
                                           #Only down carries heat
                                           "Only Down",
                                           ifelse(up > 0.01 & down <= 0.01,
                                                  #Only up carries heat
                                                  "Only Up",
                                                  ifelse(up > down,
                                                         #Up is larger
                                                         "Up",
                                                         ifelse(down > up,
                                                                #Down is larger
                                                                "Down",
                                                                "Something went wrong"))))))


#Get some feedback
cat(paste0(sum(results["direction"]=="No heat"), 
    " nodes (",
    round((sum(results["direction"]=="No heat")/nrow(results["direction"]))*100, 2),
    "%) carry no heat in both the comparisons.\n"))

cat(paste0(sum(results["direction"]=="Equal"), 
    " nodes (",
    round((sum(results["direction"]=="Equal")/nrow(results["direction"]))*100, 2),
    "%) are equal between the comparisons.\n"))

cat(paste0(sum(results["direction"]=="Up"), 
    " nodes (",
    round((sum(results["direction"]=="Up")/nrow(results["direction"]))*100, 2),
    "%) carry more heat in the up diffusion.\n"))

cat(paste0(sum(results["direction"]=="Only Up"), 
    " nodes (",
    round((sum(results["direction"]=="Only Up")/nrow(results["direction"]))*100, 2),
    "%) only have heat in the up diffusion.\n"))

cat(paste0(sum(results["direction"]=="Down"), 
    " nodes (",
    round((sum(results["direction"]=="Down")/nrow(results["direction"]))*100, 2),
    "%) nodes carry more heat in the down diffusion.\n"))

cat(paste0(sum(results["direction"]=="Only Down"), 
    " nodes (",
    round((sum(results["direction"]=="Only Down")/nrow(results["direction"]))*100, 2),
    "%) only have heat in the down diffusion.\n"))


#Send the info back to Cytoscape for visualization
loadTableData(
    results,
    data.key.column = "row.names",
    table.key.column = "display name",
    network = background_networkSuid
)
```
#Remove non-selected for singletons
```{r remove_singletons}
#Get the node table from Cytoscape
nodes <- getTableColumns(
  table = "node",
  columns = c("SUID", "name", "input"),
  network = background_networkSuid
)

#Get the edge table from Cytoscape
edges <- getTableColumns(
  table = "edge",
  columns = c("name"),
  network = background_networkSuid
)

#Extract source and target
edges$source <- substr(edges$name, start = 1, stop = 20)
edges$target <- substr(edges$name, start = 28, stop = 48)

#Identify nodes that have at least one edge
connected_nodes <- unique(c(edges$source, edges$target))

#Select the nodes that should be removed
if (REMOVE_ALL_SINGLETONS){
  #Identify singleton nodes that should be removed
  #Only remove if they are a singleton
  nodes_to_remove <- nodes %>%
    filter(
      !name %in% connected_nodes
    )
  
} else if (!REMOVE_ALL_SINGLETONS){
  #Identify singleton nodes that should be removed
  #Only remove if they are a singleton AND carry no input heat
  nodes_to_remove <- nodes %>%
    filter(
      !name %in% connected_nodes,
      input == 0
    )
  
} else {
  warning("Something unknown went wrong.\n")
}


#Select the to-be-deleted nodes
selectNodes(
    nodes_to_remove$name,
    by.col = "name",
    preserve.current.selection = FALSE,
    network = background_networkSuid
)

#Delete the singletons
RCy3::deleteSelectedNodes(network = background_networkSuid)



#Ensure the optimal zoom
RCy3::fitContent(network = background_networkSuid)

#Get the filename
file_name <- paste0(OUTPUT_FILE_LOCATION,"/Cytoscape_initial_STRING_removed_singletons")

#Export a PNG of the network
RCy3::exportImage(filename = file_name,
                  type = "PNG",
                  resolution = 600, #600 should be the maximum allowed
                  units = "inches", #inches should make the file larger
                  zoom = 500, #Use the maximum zoom possible
                  network = background_networkSuid,
                  overwriteFile = TRUE #It is allowed to overwrite the previous file (Default)
)

#Remove objects from the global environment 
rm(nodes, nodes_to_remove, edges, file_name)
```

#Functional enrichment
Note that retrieving functional enrichment manually through Cytoscape and retrieving it through code can have some differences. Notably when using the redundancy cutoff
```{r functional_enrichment}
#Get url of sting enrichment
url <- "https://string-db.org/api/json/enrichment"


if (is.null(similarity_merge_value)){
  #Don't use a similarity merge
  #Get response from the string-db instead of going through Cytoscape
    #Response is for nodes where heat ended up in both diffusions (both_nodes)
  response <- POST(
    url,
    body = list(
      identifiers = paste(both_nodes, collapse = "\r"),
      species = 9606
    ),
    encode = "form"
  )
} else if (is.double(similarity_merge_value)){
  #Do use a similarity merge
  #Get response from the string-db instead of going through Cytoscape
    #Response is for nodes where heat ended up in both diffusions (both_nodes)
  response <- POST(
    url,
    body = list(
      identifiers = paste(both_nodes, collapse = "\r"),
      species = 9606,
      merge_similarity = similarity_merge_value
    ),
    encode = "form"
  )
} else {
  warning("Something went wrong. \nStopping code.")
  stop()
}

#Get the results
response.results <- fromJSON(content(response, "text"))

#Remove the list encoding of inputGenes and preferredNames inside the df
response.results$inputGenes <- vapply(
    response.results$inputGenes,
    paste,
    collapse = " ",
    FUN.VALUE = character(1)
)
response.results$preferredNames <- vapply(
    response.results$preferredNames,
    paste,
    collapse = " ",
    FUN.VALUE = character(1)
)

#Save the results of the functional enrichment in csv files
#All functional enrichments
file_name <- paste0(OUTPUT_FILE_LOCATION,
                    "/",
                    "functional_enrichment_",
                    "all_",
                    "merged_by_",
                    ifelse(is.null(similarity_merge_value), "no_merge", similarity_merge_value),
                    ".csv")
write.csv(response.results, file_name, row.names = FALSE)

#Each category separately
for (responsetype in unique(response.results$category)){
  
  #Compose the file_name
  file_name <- paste0(OUTPUT_FILE_LOCATION,
                    "/",
                    "functional_enrichment_",
                    paste0(tolower(responsetype),"_"),
                    "merged_by_",
                    ifelse(is.null(similarity_merge_value), "no_merge", similarity_merge_value),
                    ".csv")
  
  #Save the csv
  write.csv(response.results[response.results$category == responsetype, ], 
            file_name, 
            row.names = FALSE)
}
```
